**Helper wrapping secret detection:** `check_secret(field: &str, value: &str)` in `src/memory/guard.rs`. It calls `secret_kind(value)` (also in `guard.rs`), which runs named-pattern regexes (`SECRETS` static) and a high-entropy token detector (`LONG_TOKEN` + `looks_random`). If either fires, `check_secret` returns `Refused`.

**Fields `check_secret` is applied to** — all inside the `check()` function in `src/memory/guard.rs` (lines 134–243):

| Field | Line |
|---|---|
| `text` | 146 |
| `subject` | 156 |
| `key` | 160 |
| each `tag` | 172 |
| each `ref` | 184 |
| `source` | 198 |

**Files and functions that would be affected if the credential check changed:**

- `src/memory/guard.rs`
  - `secret_kind` — the detection logic itself (regex patterns, entropy threshold in `looks_random`)
  - `check_secret` — the wrapper that calls `secret_kind` and formats the refusal; all 6 call sites flow through it
  - `check` — the top-level validation entry point that calls `check_secret` for each of the 6 fields above

- `src/memory/write.rs`
  - `Memory::remember` (line 129) — the only external caller of `guard::check`; it receives the `Refused` error and propagates it, so any change to what constitutes a credential immediately surfaces here

`docs/CONFIG.md` (line 227) documents the behaviour but contains no code.
